## [en] Short-Distance Autonomous Transport Applications

<!-- source: en/solutions/applications.md; route: /en/solutions/applications; content_type: application; status_code: design-guidance -->

---
title: Short-Distance Autonomous Transport Applications
description: Decision guide for short-distance autonomous transport in manufacturing, healthcare, retail, logistics parks, campuses and specialized sites.
status: design guidance
content_type: application
keywords: [short-distance transport, manufacturing, medical logistics, retail replenishment, logistics park, campus logistics, port, airport]
scope: Repetitive short-distance transport inside enterprises, hospitals, retail networks, logistics parks and large institutions
decision_summary: Prioritize frequent, fixed-route transport with standardized handoffs and a clear operating owner. Healthcare and specialized sites also require regulatory and safety approval.
best_for: [high-frequency repetitive transport, fixed or semi-fixed routes, trips under 5 km, standardized loading and handoff, a clear paying customer]
not_for: [infrequent transport, no stable operating owner, highly uncertain routes and handoffs, unresolved regulation or insurance, autonomous driving as a demonstration only]
next_action: Send the site, vehicle, route, shift, handoff process and compliance requirements for an application-fit assessment.
cta_url: mailto:support@wheelos.cn?subject=WheelOS%20short-distance%20transport%20assessment
---

# Short-Distance Autonomous Transport Applications

> This page is an application-selection and business-decision guide, not a performance, regulatory or safety certification. Every project must validate the site, vehicle, tasks, regulations and unit economics.

<div id="decision-summary"></div>

## Decision summary

WheelOS focuses on **frequent, repetitive, short-distance material transport** inside an enterprise or institution. The best first project is not “autonomous driving everywhere.” It is a concrete transport task that meets all of these conditions:

- A typical one-way trip is under about 5 km, mainly inside a campus, between adjacent sites or around a warehouse.
- The task repeats every day with stable shifts and a clear operating owner.
- Origins, destinations, loading areas and handoffs are relatively fixed.
- Route, vehicle, cargo, regulatory and insurance boundaries can be assessed.

<div id="scenario-priority"></div>

## Scenario priority

| Scenario | Customer task | Main value lever | Priority | Validate first |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Manufacturing | Material movement among warehouses, workshops, lines and finished-goods stores | Multi-shift labor, staffing and vehicle dispatch | Explore first | Outdoor cross-building routes, chassis, loading cadence, mixed traffic |
| Medical logistics | Specimens and supplies among hospitals, laboratories and hospital groups | Fixed time windows, repeated trips and handoff records | High value, regulated | Transport qualification, temperature, biosafety, packaging, chain of custody |
| Retail replenishment | Small-batch replenishment from a regional warehouse to nearby stores | Frequent delivery, store inventory and dispatch organization | Pilot by delivery cluster | Store density, loading windows, cold chain, urban mixed traffic |
| Logistics campus | Movement among warehouses, docks and staging areas | Central dispatch, fewer short-haul staff and less empty running | Strong fit | Site map, traffic rules, dock cadence, system interfaces |
| Campus and large venue | Food, linen, consumables and other facility tasks | Combining tasks and improving vehicle utilization | Aggregate tasks first | Task frequency, multi-building handoffs, operating owner, mixed traffic |
| Port, airport and specialized sites | Fixed shuttling and horizontal transport | Large demand, fixed area and specialized operations | Later projects | Specialized vehicles, site systems, safety access, long-term operations |

<div id="manufacturing"></div>

## 1. Manufacturing material transport

**Problem:** Raw materials, parts and work-in-progress move continuously among warehouses, workshops and production lines. Some routes are short but run many times per day.

**Typical customers:** Automotive-parts, electronics, appliance, machining and food manufacturers; industrial parks.

**Value metrics:** Trips per shift, driver and material-handler effort, vehicle waiting, on-time performance, cost per trip, night-shift and cross-building capability.

**Commercial models:** System purchase and vehicle adaptation; fixed-route monthly service; system and operations service by vehicle or shift; customer or logistics contractor vehicle ownership.

**Entry conditions:** Start with outdoor cross-building or warehouse-to-workshop routes. The production plan should make task cadence and loading demand visible instead of relying on ad-hoc dispatch.

<div id="medical-logistics"></div>

## 2. Medical and pharmaceutical transport

**Problem:** Hospitals, laboratories and hospital groups need frequent, small-batch, time-defined movement of specimens and supplies.

**Typical customers:** Hospital groups, integrated care networks, third-party medical laboratories, pharmaceutical distributors and community health centers.

**Value metrics:** Time-window compliance, trips per day, complete handoffs, exception response, manual courier effort.

**Commercial models:** Fixed-route transport contract; per-shift or service-volume settlement; technology supplied to a qualified medical-logistics operator; multi-site hospital service.

**Entry conditions:** A qualified customer or logistics partner must own transport licensing, temperature control, biosafety, packaging, chain of custody and incident handling. Autonomous driving does not replace those requirements.

<div id="retail-replenishment"></div>

## 3. Retail and chain-store replenishment

**Problem:** A regional warehouse or distribution center replenishes nearby stores frequently. Small batches reduce store inventory but increase delivery organization cost.

**Typical customers:** Convenience and fresh-food chains, supermarkets, restaurant chains, central kitchens and supply-chain companies.

**Value metrics:** Delivery timeliness, stock-out rate, cost per delivery, vehicle fill, vehicle turns and store waiting time.

**Commercial models:** Fixed store-route service; per-store, per-shift or per-task fee; vehicle leasing or capacity by usage time; centralized capacity purchase by the chain.

**Entry conditions:** Prioritize stores within about 5 km of a warehouse that can form a route cluster. Confirm loading windows, cold-chain requirements, store handoffs and the urban operating boundary.

<div id="logistics-campus"></div>

## 4. Warehouse and logistics-campus transport

**Problem:** Multiple warehouses, docks, staging areas and tenant operations create continuous short-haul transfer demand.

**Typical customers:** Warehouse operators, logistics parks, wholesale markets, supply-chain companies, bonded-zone businesses and regional distribution centers.

**Value metrics:** Transfer trips, dock waiting, empty running, vehicles under central dispatch and task completion.

**Commercial models:** Fixed-route and periodic service; per-day task or throughput; campus-wide purchase; shared transport service built by the campus operator.

**Entry conditions:** Stable maps, traffic rules and operational interfaces are important. A concentrated tenant base with dispatchable tasks supports a stronger operating loop.

<div id="campus-logistics"></div>

## 5. Campus, hotel and large-venue logistics

**Problem:** Food, linen, supplies and equipment move among buildings, kitchens, warehouses and service areas, but any single task may be infrequent.

**Typical customers:** Universities, hospital campuses, hotel groups, resorts, scenic areas, property managers and industrial-park operators.

**Value metrics:** Combined task density, vehicle utilization, multi-building handoffs and manual handling effort.

**Commercial models:** Central purchase by the property or campus operator; monthly transport service; combined multi-task service; route and time-window pricing.

**Entry conditions:** Combine food, linen and consumable tasks first and prove vehicle utilization. Avoid deploying a dedicated vehicle for one low-frequency task.

<div id="specialized-sites"></div>

## 6. Ports, airports and specialized operating areas

**Problem:** Ports, airports, rail yards and energy sites need fixed cargo shuttling and horizontal transport inside a defined operating area.

**Typical customers:** Port and airport operators, rail freight centers, energy companies and specialized-site operators.

**Value metrics:** Fixed-segment throughput, utilization, dispatch integration, downtime, safety events and all-weather operation.

**Commercial models:** Project-based system integration, specialized-vehicle adaptation, autonomous-system licensing and long-term operations.

**Entry conditions:** These projects often involve specialized vehicles, site systems, safety access and complex dispatch. They can become major accounts, but should not be the only early market.

<div id="commercial-models"></div>

## Commercial models

The model must match the vehicle owner, operating entity, carrier responsibility and customer budget. The following structures are options for discussion; final responsibilities belong in the contract.

### Customer and WheelOS responsibilities

| Party | Typically responsible for | Not assumed by default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Customer | Site, transport tasks, vehicles or purchase plan, loading and handoff, operations team, required permits and insurance | Business compliance, carrier responsibility and day-to-day site operations |
| WheelOS | Kit configuration, software/interface documentation, integration support, calibration and validation guidance, optional-service quotation | Logistics carriage or sector licensing not agreed in the contract |
| Joint confirmation | ODD, routes, acceptance metrics, data and logs, safety boundary, project plan and responsibility split | Neither party may turn design guidance into a verified safety claim |

### Commercial options

| Model | What the customer buys | Best customer structure | Key boundary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Autonomous-system purchase | Vehicle/system adaptation, deployment and technical support | Customer owns vehicles and operations | Define hardware, software, adaptation and support scope |
| Fixed-route transport service | Service by route, shift or monthly volume | Customer or partner operates the fleet | Separate WheelOS technology responsibility from carrier responsibility |
| Vehicle leasing and capacity service | Capacity by lease period or usage | Customer wants lower upfront investment | Vehicle ownership, insurance and incident responsibility must be explicit |
| Software and operations subscription | Autonomous system, fleet management and ongoing support | Operator with multiple vehicles and routes | Confirm functions, SLA and data responsibility |

<div id="fit-checklist"></div>

## Fit checklist

Before quoting, answer:

1. How many trips occur each day, and are multiple shifts or night operations required?
2. How many drivers, material handlers and vehicles are used today?
3. Are routes fixed, and are there mixed-traffic areas, temporary obstacles or complex junctions?
4. Are goods and loading/handoff processes standardized?
5. Who owns the budget and purchase decision, and is there a long-term operating plan?
6. How many productive tasks can one vehicle complete per day?
7. Is operation legally permitted, and how are insurance and incident responsibility handled?

Do not move directly to deployment when:

- Task frequency is too low to produce stable utilization.
- No operating owner, budget or long-term plan exists.
- Origins, destinations, loading or handoffs are highly uncertain.
- Regulation, insurance or site safety responsibility remains unresolved.
- The customer asks only for a “driverless demonstration” without a business metric.

<div id="what-wheelos-provides"></div>

## What WheelOS provides

<div class="solution-grid">
  <div class="solution-card">
    <span class="solution-card__index">01 / KIT</span>
    <h3>Integrated Autonomous Driving Kit</h3>
    <p>Pre-integrated compute, sensors, GNSS/INS, software and developer tools for low-speed campus project development and integration.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="solution-card">
    <span class="solution-card__index">02 / ADAPT</span>
    <h3>Vehicle and site adaptation</h3>
    <p>Project configuration and integration services around chassis CAN, routes, loading, calibration and validation.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="solution-card">
    <span class="solution-card__index">03 / OPERATE</span>
    <h3>Operations planning</h3>
    <p>Vehicle onboarding, fleet management and remote monitoring are project-planning topics; functions, SLA and delivery conditions require confirmation.</p>
  </div>
</div>

WheelOS does not operate parcel collection, sorting, last-mile delivery or parcel stations, and does not replace the compliance responsibilities of healthcare, port or airport operators.

<div id="next-steps"></div>

## Next steps

1. Share the site, vehicle, routes, shifts, cargo and handoff process.
2. Screen task frequency, operating owner, regulation and unit economics together.
3. Review chassis, sensor placement, site map, safety and acceptance metrics.
4. Run a minimum integration and validation project in a controlled environment.

## [zh-CN] 自动驾驶项目交付与试点流程

<!-- source: solutions/delivery-process.md; route: /solutions/delivery-process; content_type: delivery; status_code: design-guidance -->

---
title: 自动驾驶项目交付与试点流程
description: 像建房子一样展示自动驾驶短途运输项目的场景调研、方案设计、集成、验证、试点和规模化过程。
status: 设计建议
content_type: delivery
keywords: [交付流程, 试点, 现场调研, 集成, 标定, 验证, 运营指标, 证据包]
scope: WheelOS 短途自动驾驶运输项目的规划与交付方法
decision_summary: 把项目拆成可检查的阶段，每个阶段都有客户可见交付物、通过条件和未验证边界；未通过前一阶段不进入下一阶段。
best_for: [受控场景试点, 固定路线运输, 车辆和底盘集成, 可量化运营指标]

# 自动驾驶项目交付与试点流程

> 自动驾驶项目更适合像建房子一样推进：先勘察地基，再设计和施工，最后验收和入住。每一步都应该能看到成果、问题和证据，而不是先卖一个“成品”，再让客户承担集成风险。

## 客户看到的七个阶段

| 阶段 | 客户能看到什么 | 关键交付物 | 进入下一阶段的条件 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1. 场景调研 | 任务、班次、路线、货物、交接和当前成本 | 场景筛选表和初步价值测算 | 高频、可运营、有明确负责人 |
| 2. 边界设计 | 运行设计域、站点、路线、风险和法规问题 | 项目边界、责任矩阵和初步验收指标 | 风险可接受且责任明确 |
| 3. 车辆与传感器 | 底盘、传感器布局、计算平台和接口 | 硬件配置、接口清单和安装方案 | 线控和关键 CAN 信号可确认 |
| 4. 软件与数据集成 | 时间同步、坐标、定位、感知、规划和控制链路 | 配置、标定记录、数据记录和系统检查表 | 数据链路和基础功能可回放 |
| 5. 回放与受控场地验证 | 测试场景、指标、失败样本和问题清单 | 验证报告、失败案例和修复记录 | 达到约定阈值且边界清楚 |
| 6. 试点运行 | 每日任务、人员分工、异常处理和运营看板 | 运行日志、KPI、异常闭环和阶段总结 | 能稳定运营并按约定收集证据 |
| 7. 评估与扩展 | 是否具备复制条件、成本和风险 | 证据包、复盘和扩展建议 | 有可复核结果和明确剩余风险 |

## 每阶段都要“看得见”

### 客户可以要求查看

- 现场照片、路线图和运行设计域。
- 传感器与底盘接口清单。
- 时间同步、标定和数据记录检查结果。
- 回放数据、场景清单、指标和失败样本。
- 问题清单、修复记录和未解决风险。
- 试点运营看板和阶段复盘。

### WheelOS 应提供

- 明确的项目阶段和负责人。
- 每个阶段的输入、输出和验收条件。
- 标准配置、接口文档和测试记录格式。
- 技术风险、依赖和未验证边界。
- 可追溯的版本、配置和证据索引。

## 试点必须记录的指标

| 指标 | 建议先定义的基线 | 用途 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 运输频次 | 每日任务数、班次和高峰时段 | 判断真实需求和车辆利用率 |
| 人工投入 | 司机、搬运、调度和人工干预小时 | 与试点后的投入比较 |
| 车辆利用率 | 有效运行时间、等待时间和空驶时间 | 判断单车经济性 |
| 准点率 | 按约定时间窗口完成任务的比例 | 衡量业务可用性 |
| 异常次数 | 每百次任务的接管、急停、路径阻塞和人工恢复 | 识别系统与流程薄弱点 |
| 单位成本 | 每次任务、每公里或每个托盘的运营成本 | 判断商业可行性 |
| 安全事件 | 分级记录碰撞、险情、违规和现场风险 | 触发停机和整改 |

这些是试点评价指标，不是 WheelOS 已实现的性能数据。只有在实际项目中记录并复核后，才能产生证据。

## 不跳阶段

- 底盘和线控接口未确认，不进入车辆集成承诺。
- 时间同步、坐标和标定未检查，不进入路线性能结论。
- 没有回放和失败样本，不进入场地验证结论。
- 没有基线和运营指标，不进入商业效果结论。
- 没有完整证据记录，不把试点升级为“已验证”或量产能力。

## 试点结束时应形成的证据包

1. 任务和运行设计域。
2. 软件、配置、车辆和传感器版本。
3. 原始日志、录包和关键回放。
4. 基线、目标值、实际指标和统计方法。
5. 异常、接管、失败样本和整改记录。
6. 未覆盖场景、法规边界和剩余风险。
7. 复核人和下一阶段建议。

  </div>

## [en] Autonomous Project Delivery and Pilot Process

<!-- source: en/solutions/delivery-process.md; route: /en/solutions/delivery-process; content_type: delivery; status_code: design-guidance -->

---
title: Autonomous Project Delivery and Pilot Process
description: A transparent, house-building-style process for autonomous short-distance transport projects from discovery through integration, validation, pilot and scale.
status: design guidance
content_type: delivery
keywords: [delivery process, pilot, site assessment, integration, calibration, validation, operations metrics, evidence pack]
scope: Planning and delivery method for WheelOS short-distance autonomous transport projects
decision_summary: Break the project into reviewable stages with customer-visible deliverables, exit criteria and unresolved boundaries. Do not advance without passing the previous gate.
best_for: [controlled-site pilots, fixed-route transport, vehicle and chassis integration, measurable operating metrics]
not_for: [deployment without site assessment, operating commitments before chassis confirmation, production claims without evidence]
next_action: Start with application discovery and define the task, operating boundary, vehicle conditions, acceptance metrics and stage owners.
cta_url: mailto:support@wheelos.cn?subject=WheelOS%20pilot%20delivery%20plan
---

# Autonomous Project Delivery and Pilot Process

> An autonomous-driving project is easier to trust when it is built like a house: inspect the ground first, then design, build, inspect and move in. Customers should see outputs, issues and evidence at each step instead of buying an opaque “finished product” and inheriting the integration risk.

## Seven customer-visible stages

| Stage | What the customer sees | Key deliverables | Gate to continue |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Application discovery | Tasks, shifts, routes, cargo, handoffs and current cost | Application screen and preliminary value case | Frequent work, operable demand and a clear owner |
| 2. Boundary design | ODD, stops, routes, risks and regulatory issues | Project boundary, responsibility matrix and draft acceptance metrics | Risks acceptable and responsibilities explicit |
| 3. Vehicle and sensors | Chassis, sensor placement, compute and interfaces | Hardware configuration, interface list and installation plan | Drive-by-wire and critical CAN signals confirmed |
| 4. Software and data integration | Time sync, frames, localization, perception, planning and control path | Configuration, calibration records, data recording and system checklist | Data path and baseline functions are replayable |
| 5. Replay and controlled-site validation | Test scenarios, metrics, failure samples and issue list | Validation report, failure cases and fix records | Agreed thresholds met and boundaries documented |
| 6. Pilot operation | Daily tasks, staffing, exception handling and operations dashboard | Operating logs, KPIs, issue closure and stage review | Stable operation and evidence collection |
| 7. Assessment and expansion | Whether the solution is repeatable, cost-effective and safe to extend | Evidence pack, retrospective and expansion recommendation | Reviewable results and explicit residual risk |

## Make every stage visible

### The customer should be able to inspect

- Site photos, route map and operating design domain.
- Sensor and chassis-interface lists.
- Time-sync, calibration and data-recording checks.
- Replay data, scenario list, metrics and failure samples.
- Issue list, fixes and unresolved risks.
- Pilot dashboard and stage retrospective.

### WheelOS should provide

- Explicit project stages and owners.
- Inputs, outputs and acceptance conditions for each stage.
- Standard configurations, interface documentation and test-record formats.
- Technical risks, dependencies and unverified boundaries.
- Traceable versions, configuration and evidence indexes.

## Metrics every pilot must record

| Metric | Baseline to define first | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Transport frequency | Tasks per day, shifts and peak windows | Test real demand and vehicle utilization |
| Labor input | Driver, material-handler, dispatch and intervention hours | Compare with the post-pilot process |
| Vehicle utilization | Productive run time, waiting and empty running | Assess single-vehicle economics |
| On-time rate | Tasks completed inside the agreed window | Measure operational availability |
| Exceptions | Interventions, emergency stops, blocked paths and manual recovery per 100 tasks | Expose system and process weaknesses |
| Unit cost | Cost per task, kilometer or pallet | Assess commercial viability |
| Safety events | Collisions, near misses, violations and site risks, classified | Trigger stop and corrective action |

These are pilot-evaluation metrics, not current WheelOS performance measurements. Evidence exists only after an actual project records and reviews them.

## Do not skip stages

- Do not commit to vehicle integration before chassis and drive-by-wire interfaces are confirmed.
- Do not infer route performance before time sync, frames and calibration are checked.
- Do not make site-validation conclusions without replay and failure samples.
- Do not make business-impact conclusions without a baseline and operating metrics.
- Do not upgrade a pilot to “verified” or a production capability without a complete evidence record.

## Evidence pack at pilot close

1. Task definition and operating design domain.
2. Software, configuration, vehicle and sensor versions.
3. Raw logs, recordings and critical replays.
4. Baseline, target, actual metrics and statistical method.
5. Exceptions, interventions, failure samples and corrective actions.
6. Uncovered scenarios, regulatory boundary and residual risk.
7. Reviewer and next-stage recommendation.

## 适用场景

| 场景 | 典型车辆 | 项目重点 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 工业制造 | 厂内物流车、物料运输车 | 多班次运输、装卸节拍、跨厂房路线 |
| 医疗物资 | 样本与物资运输车 | 固定时限、交接记录、合规条件 |
| 商业零售 | 门店补货车、配送车辆 | 小批量多频次、装卸窗口、线路集群 |
| 仓储物流园区 | 短驳车、牵引/运输平台 | 月台作业、统一调度、园区规则 |
| 校园与大型园区 | 后勤物资运输车 | 多任务合并、楼宇交接、单车利用率 |
| 港口机场与专用区域 | 专用运输车辆 | 场地系统、安全准入、项目集成 |

## 核心解决方案

### 一体化自动驾驶开发套件

以 NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin 32G 域控制器为核心，集成 16 线激光雷达、4 路环视相机、RTK GNSS + IMU 组合导航和基础自动驾驶软件栈。适合希望在封闭或半封闭场景中快速建立原型、开展算法验证和进行车辆联调的团队。

**参考价格：人民币 39,900 元起。** 最终配置、运费、税费和可选服务以正式报价为准。

[查看完整规格、交付清单与集成要求 →](/solutions/integrated-autonomous-driving-kit)

## Featured solution

### Integrated Autonomous Driving Kit

A development kit built around the NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin 32G platform, with a 16-line LiDAR, four surround cameras, RTK GNSS + IMU and a baseline autonomous-driving stack. It is designed for teams that need to establish a prototype, validate algorithms and integrate a vehicle in a controlled environment.

**Reference price: from RMB 39,900.** Final configuration, freight, taxes and optional services are confirmed in a formal quotation.

## 系统组成

<div class="solution-flow" role="img" aria-label="系统数据流：传感器与底盘进入时间同步和数据接口，再进入定位、感知、规划与控制，最终输出到底盘执行">
  <div class="solution-flow__node"><strong>传感器与底盘</strong><span>LiDAR · Camera · GNSS/INS</span></div>
  <span class="solution-flow__arrow" aria-hidden="true">→</span>
  <div class="solution-flow__node"><strong>时间同步与接口</strong><span>PTP/gPTP · CAN FD · Ethernet</span></div>
  <span class="solution-flow__arrow" aria-hidden="true">→</span>
  <div class="solution-flow__node"><strong>自动驾驶软件栈</strong><span>Localization · Perception · Planning</span></div>
  <span class="solution-flow__arrow" aria-hidden="true">→</span>
  <div class="solution-flow__node"><strong>车辆执行</strong><span>Control · Steer · Drive · Brake</span></div>
</div>

套件以高性能自动驾驶域控制器为核心，融合 LiDAR、相机和组合导航等多源数据，通过标准接口与车辆线控底盘交互。软件栈可基于 Apollo，也可采用自有 WheelOS 框架。

## 规格概览

### 自动驾驶域控制器

| 参数 | 规格 |
| --- | --- |
| 计算核心 | NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin 32G |
| AI 算力 | 200 TOPS INT8 |
| 内存 | 32 GB LPDDR5，204.8 GB/s |
| 存储 | 512 GB NVMe 2280 SSD |
| 核心接口 | 2 × CAN（支持 CAN FD）；8 × GMSL2；4 × 以太网 LiDAR 接口 |
| 辅助接口 | 1 × USB 3.0；3 × UART（RS232/485 可配置）；GPIO；1 × HDMI 2.0 |
| 同步与可靠性 | 硬件级 PTP/gPTP Master/Slave；硬件看门狗；可选安全 MCU |
| 供电 | 9–36 V DC 宽压输入，带反接和过压保护 |
| 功耗与环境 | 典型功耗约 80 W；工作温度 -20°C 至 +60°C；IP65 |
| 散热 | 被动散热 + 智能风扇辅助 |

### 标准传感器

| 传感器 | 规格 |
| --- | --- |
| 主激光雷达 | 16 线机械旋转式；360° 水平视场；约 30° 垂直视场；≥120 m@10% 反射率；10 Hz；测距精度 ±3 cm；以太网；IP67 |
| 环视相机 | 4 × 车规级广角相机；水平视场 ≥120°；1280 × 720；≥30 fps；≥100 dB HDR；GMSL2；IP67 |
| 相机选项 | 可选 190° 鱼眼镜头和 1920 × 1080 分辨率 |
| 组合导航 | RTK GNSS + 工业级 IMU；支持 GPS/GLONASS/BeiDou/Galileo；更新率 ≥100 Hz；UART/CAN/以太网 |
| 连接配置 | 5G 与 Wi-Fi 6 路由器、4 个千兆网口，可根据项目确认 |

## 软件与开发工具

| 模块 | 提供内容 |
| --- | --- |
| 基础软件 | Ubuntu 20.04 / 22.04 LTS（经实时性优化）、Apollo Cyber RT 中间件 |
| 感知 | LiDAR 与 Camera 前融合/后融合 3D 目标检测与跟踪，覆盖车辆、行人、二轮车 |
| 定位 | 融合 RTK-GNSS、IMU 和 LiDAR SLAM，输出高精度、高频率车辆位姿 |
| 规划与控制 | 高精地图点到点路径规划、静态障碍物避障、速度规划；PID/LQR 控制框架与 CAN 底盘接口 |
| 工具链 | 传感器在线/离线标定、DreamView 可视化、Cyber Record 记录与回放、HMI 示例 |
| 开发接口 | C++/Python SDK，包含消息订阅、数据录制、控制下发接口、API 文档和示例代码 |
| 仿真接口（可选） | 面向 CARLA、SVL 等平台的集成接口，支持 SIL/HIL 测试验证 |

## 标准交付清单

| 类别 | 内容 |
| --- | --- |
| 硬件 | 1 × 自动驾驶域控制器；1 × 16 线激光雷达；4 × 环视相机；1 × 组合导航（含天线）；标准线缆与必要附件 |
| 软件 | 预装 Ubuntu、Cyber RT、基础版自动驾驶软件栈、开发与调试工具 |
| 文档 | 产品规格书、用户手册、快速入门指南、API/SDK 参考文档 |
| 支持 | 自购买之日起 1 个月免费远程技术支持，覆盖安装、配置和基本使用问题 |

## 底盘与集成要求

车辆应具备开放、稳定、响应及时的 CAN 总线控制接口，至少包括：

- 转向角度或角速度控制
- 油门或驱动力矩控制
- 制动压力或减速度控制
- 档位状态与必要的车辆状态反馈
- 可确认的通信协议、信号定义、单位和安全限制

推荐集成流程：

1. **需求与接口确认：**明确场景、路线、速度、车辆约束、验收指标和底盘 CAN 能力。
2. **台架与车辆集成：**完成传感器安装、时间同步、内外参标定和底盘接口联调。
3. **数据与算法验证：**采集典型路线数据，通过回放、场景测试和指标分析迭代参数。
4. **现场测试与交接：**在受控场地验证基础功能，完成文档、培训和问题闭环。

## 服务与定制

| 服务 | 是否包含 | 说明 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 标准文档与远程支持 | 包含 | 1 个月免费远程技术支持 |
| 现场部署与精标定 | 可选 | 硬件安装、传感器内外参、车辆动力学参数、系统联调和基础功能演示 |
| 定制化培训 | 可选 | 系统架构、算法原理、二次开发、测试运维 |
| 功能定制开发 | 可选 | 针对场景需求开发算法模块或扩展功能 |
| 高精度地图服务 | 可选 | 园区地图采集、生产与维护 |
| 仿真测试服务 | 可选 | 基于仿真平台的算法测试与验证 |

## 常见问题

### 套件是否包含车辆底盘？

不包含。套件提供域控制器、传感器、软件和服务，车辆需具备符合要求的线控底盘与 CAN 控制接口。

### 能否适配我们现有的车辆？

需要先核对底盘通信协议、控制信号、响应特性、安装空间和车辆安全限制。建议在报价前提供 CAN DBC、车辆尺寸、传感器布置约束和目标场景。

### 是否可以用于量产项目？

本套件定位于原型开发、测试验证和受控场景集成。量产项目需另行完成功能安全、法规准入、可靠性和供应链要求评估。

### 支持哪些语言和地区？

本站提供中文和英文产品资料，可接受海外项目询价。交付范围、语言支持、现场服务和适用法规会在项目评估时确认。

## Why start with a pre-integrated kit

<div class="solution-grid">
  <div class="solution-card">
    <span class="solution-card__index">01</span>
    <h3>Reduce integration work</h3>
    <p>Compute, sensors, cabling and software modules share a defined interface, reducing hardware selection, driver adaptation and data-path debugging.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="solution-card">
    <span class="solution-card__index">02</span>
    <h3>Keep the platform open</h3>
    <p>Use the C++/Python SDK, API documentation, examples and CAN control interface to connect your own algorithms or operations system.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="solution-card">
    <span class="solution-card__index">03</span>
    <h3>Investigate with evidence</h3>
    <p>Record and replay Cyber Record data, inspect system state in DreamView and calibrate sensors as part of a traceable workflow.</p>
  </div>
</div>

## System architecture

<div class="solution-flow" role="img" aria-label="System data flow from sensors and chassis through time synchronization and data interfaces, into localization, perception and planning, then to steering, drive and brake control">
  <div class="solution-flow__node"><strong>Sensors & chassis</strong><span>LiDAR · Camera · GNSS/INS</span></div>
  <span class="solution-flow__arrow" aria-hidden="true">→</span>
  <div class="solution-flow__node"><strong>Sync & interfaces</strong><span>PTP/gPTP · CAN FD · Ethernet</span></div>
  <span class="solution-flow__arrow" aria-hidden="true">→</span>
  <div class="solution-flow__node"><strong>Autonomy stack</strong><span>Localization · Perception · Planning</span></div>
  <span class="solution-flow__arrow" aria-hidden="true">→</span>
  <div class="solution-flow__node"><strong>Vehicle actuation</strong><span>Control · Steer · Drive · Brake</span></div>
</div>

The kit combines multi-sensor data from LiDAR, cameras and GNSS/INS on an autonomous-driving domain controller. A standard vehicle interface connects the software stack to a drive-by-wire chassis. The stack can be based on Apollo or the WheelOS framework.

## Specifications

### Autonomous driving domain controller

| Parameter | Specification |
| --- | --- |
| Compute module | NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin 32G |
| AI performance | 200 TOPS INT8 |
| Memory | 32 GB LPDDR5, 204.8 GB/s |
| Storage | 512 GB NVMe 2280 SSD |
| Core interfaces | 2 × CAN with CAN FD support; 8 × GMSL2; 4 × Ethernet LiDAR ports |
| Additional interfaces | 1 × USB 3.0; 3 × UART (RS232/485 configurable); GPIO; 1 × HDMI 2.0 |
| Synchronization and reliability | Hardware PTP/gPTP master/slave; hardware watchdog; optional safety MCU |
| Power | 9–36 V DC wide input with reverse-polarity and overvoltage protection |
| Power and environment | Approx. 80 W typical; -20°C to +60°C operating temperature; IP65 |
| Cooling | Passive cooling plus intelligent fan assist |

### Standard sensor suite

| Sensor | Specification |
| --- | --- |
| Primary LiDAR | 16-line mechanical rotating scanner; 360° horizontal field of view; approx. 30° vertical field of view; ≥120 m at 10% reflectivity; 10 Hz; ±3 cm ranging accuracy; Ethernet; IP67 |
| Surround cameras | 4 × automotive-grade wide-angle cameras; ≥120° horizontal field of view; 1280 × 720; ≥30 fps; ≥100 dB HDR; GMSL2; IP67 |
| Camera options | Optional 190° fisheye lens and 1920 × 1080 resolution |
| GNSS/INS | RTK GNSS + industrial IMU; GPS/GLONASS/BeiDou/Galileo; ≥100 Hz update rate; UART/CAN/Ethernet |
| Connectivity configuration | 5G and Wi-Fi 6 router with 4 × gigabit Ethernet ports, subject to project confirmation |

## Software and tools

| Module | What is provided |
| --- | --- |
| Base software | Ubuntu 20.04 / 22.04 LTS with real-time tuning; Apollo Cyber RT middleware |
| Perception | LiDAR and camera early/late fusion for 3D detection and tracking of vehicles, pedestrians and two-wheelers |
| Localization | Fusion of RTK-GNSS, IMU and LiDAR SLAM for high-rate, high-accuracy vehicle pose |
| Planning and control | HD-map point-to-point routing, static-obstacle avoidance and speed planning; PID/LQR control framework and CAN chassis interface |
| Tooling | Online/offline sensor calibration, DreamView visualization, Cyber Record recording and replay, HMI examples |
| Developer interfaces | C++/Python SDK for message subscription, data recording and control commands, with API documentation and examples |
| Simulation interfaces (optional) | Integration interfaces for CARLA, SVL and similar platforms for SIL/HIL validation |

## Standard deliverables

| Category | Included |
| --- | --- |
| Hardware | 1 × autonomous-driving domain controller; 1 × 16-line LiDAR; 4 × surround cameras; 1 × GNSS/INS with antenna; standard cable set and required accessories |
| Software | Preinstalled Ubuntu, Cyber RT, baseline autonomous-driving stack and development/debugging tools |
| Documentation | Product specification, user manual, quick-start guide and API/SDK reference |
| Support | One month of remote technical support from purchase, covering installation, configuration and basic use |

## Chassis and integration requirements

The vehicle should provide an open, stable and responsive CAN control interface with at least:

- Steering angle or steering-rate control
- Throttle or drive-torque control
- Brake-pressure or deceleration control
- Gear state and required vehicle-status feedback
- Confirmed communication protocol, signal definitions, units and safety limits

Recommended integration sequence:

1. **Scope and interface review:** define the site, route, speed, vehicle constraints, acceptance criteria and chassis CAN capabilities.
2. **Bench and vehicle integration:** install sensors, verify time synchronization, calibrate intrinsics/extrinsics and connect the chassis interface.
3. **Data and algorithm validation:** record representative routes, replay data, run scenario tests and iterate parameters against measurable criteria.
4. **Controlled test and handover:** validate baseline functions at a controlled site, complete documentation, training and issue closure.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is a vehicle chassis included?

No. The kit includes the domain controller, sensors, software and support. The vehicle project supplies a compatible drive-by-wire chassis and CAN interface.

### Can the kit be integrated with our existing vehicle?

We first review the chassis protocol, control signals, response behavior, installation space and vehicle safety limits. For an efficient quotation, share the CAN DBC, vehicle dimensions, sensor-placement constraints and target operating scenario.

### Can it be used in a production vehicle program?

The kit is intended for prototype development, test validation and controlled-site integration. A production program requires separate functional-safety, regulatory, reliability and supply-chain qualification.

### Do you work with international customers?

Yes. English product documentation and international project inquiries are supported. Delivery scope, language support, on-site service and applicable regulations are confirmed during project evaluation.
